title: A bounded type
summary: <T extends Comparable<T>> lets a generic method compare its items.

steps.title: When any type is too many

say.never: With a plain `<T>`, Java knows nothing about `T`, so it can't let you call `compareTo` on it: not every type can be compared. A **bound** narrows the blank. `<T extends Comparable<T>>` means "any type T, as long as a T can be compared with another T". `Integer`, `Double` and `String` all qualify, so they're all allowed.
say.bit: A **bound**, `<T extends Comparable<T>>`, allows only types that can be compared, so you can call `compareTo`.

say.never: `a.compareTo(b)` answers with a number. **Negative** means `a` comes before `b` (it's smaller). **Zero** means they're equal. **Positive** means `a` comes after `b` (it's bigger). For numbers that's size; for `String`s it's alphabetical order. Compare the answer with 0, never with 1 or -1, since the number can be any size.
say.bit: `compareTo`: negative = smaller, 0 = equal, positive = bigger. Compare it with 0.

steps.title: In your lesson: When any type is too many

say.never: `max` finds the biggest item in a list of anything comparable: the best score, the longest distance, the last auto name alphabetically. Remember the first item as the best so far. Then replace it only when an item is *bigger* (`compareTo` is more than 0), so a tie keeps the first one. Return `null` for an empty list.
say.bit: `max`: start with the first item; swap only when `compareTo` is more than 0; `null` if empty.
